fixes.title: Per-event routing claims it will deliver to Email/Telegram/MQTT that the same page knows are unconfigured
fixes.summary: Added configuredNotificationTransportsProvider (skotiq_core) which reports exactly the transport kinds whose config `isConfigured` is true - the same predicate NotificationRouter._eligibleTransports uses to silently drop a transport at send time (systemPush maps to the push master gate, inApp is always available). The routing page now watches it and names any other transport for what it is: the per-category summary row renders '-> In-app banner + Email (SMTP) (not configured) + Telegram (not configured)', the editor's FilterChips carry the same suffix, and ticking one adds an inline warning ('Telegram is not configured, so this rule will not reach you there. Set the credentials up under Transports below.'). The row can no longer assert a channel that would deliver nothing.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/notification_routing_unconfigured_transport_test.dart -> 4 tests (picker names channels that cannot deliver / selecting one says it will not reach you / saved summary row marks them / a configured transport is presented plainly)
fixes.revert_check: Replaced the body of _transportLabel (notification_routing_settings.dart) with `=> kind.label;` -> 3 of 4 tests FAILED; the 4th (configured transport) still passed, which is the control. Restored -> 4/4 pass, plus notification_routing_settings_test.dart 5/5.
fixes.caveats: The provider is a new addition to a shared core file; no existing core code path reads it. Shared-file gate: the whole skotiq_core suite ran (5382 passed, 23 failed) and the whole skotiq_app suite ran (2794 passed, 46 failed); every failure is in an untouched area - imaging_service_test (sqlite 'idx_profiles_name already exists' from parallel isolates, the known cold-start flake), nina_sequence_fidelity_test (another agent's in-flight importer validation), and the golden/captures_landscape pixel tests plus a path_provider MissingPluginException.

fixes.title: Dead/duplicated settings keys persist and are exported while no UI reflects them
fixes.summary: Both cases were closed by an earlier wave; I confirmed each in the current tree rather than re-fixing. Case 1 (auto_save_sequences): the key is gone from _defaultSettings and now sits in _retiredSettingKeys (default_settings.dart:144-157), which schema_helpers._pruneRetiredSettings() DELETEs from app_settings on EVERY open (wired at migration_strategy.dart:32), so an already-created profile stops exporting it too; retired_settings_prune_test.dart asserts both the fresh-profile absence and the prune of a hand-inserted row. Case 2 (plate_solver): the sqlite row is now an explicitly-documented projection of the native PlateSolverPreference - default seeded 'Auto' to match the native default (default_settings.dart:21-25), refreshed from plateSolveService.getConfig() on every settings load (app_settings_notifier._refreshPlateSolverProjection, :262-293), re-synced immediately on save (plate_solver_provider.updatePreference -> syncPlateSolverFromPreference, :154-176), and pinned against remote snapshots (app_settings_notifier:578-590) so a partial POST cannot announce an engine switch. plate_solver_single_store_test.dart covers it.
fixes.revert_check: n/a - nothing changed this wave. Evidence is the code above plus the two existing tests.
fixes.caveats: The verifier's note that _resolveSolverId() reads settings.plateSolver still holds, but it now reads a value that is refreshed from the native preference on load and on save, so the label and the engine agree.

fixes.title: Editing a settings dropdown fires a CRITICAL 'Safe the rig' alert on a completely idle app, and the alert text contradicts itself
fixes.summary: Half of this was already closed by an earlier wave: safe_rig_service._emitNotification no longer says 'Rig safed: no action was possible' - when no step did anything it posts a WARNING reading 'Nothing to safe: ...'. What was still open is the finding's item (1): the safing WORKFLOW still ran off a settings edit on an idle app. WeatherSafetyNotifier._enforceSafetyActions now asks _hasAnythingToSafe() first - a pausable sequence, an armed secondary rig, or a connected mount / dome / cover, i.e. exactly the union of conditions under which SafeRigService.safeTheRig issues a command on the weather path. When none holds it skips the workflow and posts one warning per unsafe episode instead ('<reason>. No run is active and no mount, dome or cover is connected, so nothing was commanded. Weather safety will act as soon as equipment is connected or a run starts.'). Deliberately NOT latched: it returns false so the episode stays re-armed and the next evaluation safes the rig the moment a mount or a run appears while conditions are still unsafe. An unreadable secondary-rig status errs towards enforcing.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/weather_safety_nothing_to_safe_test.dart -> 4 tests: idle+disconnected rig is not safed and gets a warning (not 'Rig safed'), the disclosure is not repeated across re-evaluations, a connected mount IS still safed, an armed secondary rig IS still safed
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the whole `if (!await _hasAnythingToSafe()) { ... return false; }` block from _enforceSafetyActions (the production call site, not the helper) -> tests 1 and 2 FAILED with `Expected: empty  Actual: ['No weather data sources available']` (safeTheRig executed again); tests 3 and 4, the anti-inversion controls, still passed. Restored -> 4/4 pass.
fixes.caveats: The two control tests exist specifically to catch the inversion this fix could have introduced (a gate that stops a REAL safing). The 'nothing to safe' path now costs one secondary-rig status read per 5-minute evaluation while the episode lasts, instead of latching after one attempt. Shared-file gate: the whole skotiq_core suite ran (5382 passed, 23 failed) and the whole skotiq_app suite ran (2794 passed, 46 failed); every failure is in an untouched area - imaging_service_test (sqlite 'idx_profiles_name already exists' from parallel isolates, the known cold-start flake), nina_sequence_fidelity_test (another agent's in-flight importer validation), and the golden/captures_landscape pixel tests plus a path_provider MissingPluginException.

fixes.title: PHD2 Guiding settings has no way to test the connection
fixes.summary: Added a 'Test connection' row to the PHD2 Guiding page that probes the configured endpoint through the existing GuidingBackend.isPhd2Running (the same call onboarding's Guider step makes, so it works against a remote imaging host too) and renders the outcome inline next to a success/error icon: 'PHD2 answered on localhost:4400.' or 'No response on localhost:4400. Is PHD2 running with "Enable Server" turned on?'. The result is keyed to the host:port it actually used, so editing the host/port drops a stale 'answered' rather than showing it against a different address, and a backend switch mid-probe discards the answer. Deliberately NOT rebuilt: Phd2Launcher and the onboarding tester already exist (the verifier's location_wrong note), so this only closes the missing affordance on the page that configures it.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/phd2_test_connection_test.dart -> 3 tests (the row exists and names the endpoint / a reachable PHD2 is reported reached, with isPhd2Running verified called once with host+port / a silent socket reports the cause)
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the entire 'Test connection' SettingRow from phd2_guiding_settings.dart (severing the call site, not just the logic) -> all 3 tests FAILED. Restored -> 3/3 pass.
fixes.caveats: No PHD2 version or profile readout: the bridge exposes api_phd2_get_profile but no GuidingBackend method does, and wiring it would mean changing the role interface plus all three backend implementations for a P3 parity gap. The executable-path row still shows the configured path without probing it.

fixes.title: Fail-closed is the shipped default and the Weather Safety page never tells a sensorless rig what that means
fixes.summary: The Weather Safety page now carries both missing facts, immediately under the master switch it owns. A 'Safety sources' row states the live three-state read of each source ('Weather device: reporting safe · Safety monitor: connected, not reporting') or, when there is none, 'No weather device or safety monitor is connected. With Fail Closed (Park), missing data counts as unsafe: a run will refuse to start and the rig is parked.' - and with the master switch off it carries the existing '- inactive until "Enable weather safety" is on' suffix. A 'Safety fail mode' dropdown sits next to it, writing the same appSettings value the Sequencer page writes. To keep the two pages from describing one stored mode differently, the label/description strings moved into one SafetyFailModeLabels extension that both now use. The readings come from a new weatherSafetySourceReadingsProvider in core, built on readHardwareWeatherSource / readSafetyMonitorSource - the evaluator's own rules, lifted from private methods to top-level functions with no behaviour change - so the page cannot count a source the enforcement path has written off as stale. Deliberately NOT done: the finding's suggestion to auto-switch a sensorless rig to Warn Only. Silently rewriting a safety policy because the operator armed it is the inversion this campaign keeps catching; the fail mode is now visible and changeable one row away instead.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/weather_safety_sources_disclosure_test.dart -> 5 widget tests over the rendered rows (sensorless copy + fail-closed consequence / fail mode selectable here / fail-open states its own consequence / connected sources reported by reading / master-switch-off prerequisite); packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/weather_safety_source_readings_test.dart -> 5 provider tests (absent / connected-but-never-reported = unknown / in-threshold = safe / past-threshold = unsafe / stale = unknown not safe)
fixes.revert_check: Replaced WeatherSafetyPolicyRows.build's returned Column of the two SettingRows with `const Column(children: [])` -> all 5 widget tests FAILED. Restored -> 5/5 pass. Core provider test: it is new coverage of a moved-but-unchanged rule, and the whole skotiq_core suite was run because the extraction touched a shared file.
fixes.caveats: The widget test pumps WeatherSafetyPolicyRows, not the whole WeatherSafetySettings page: pumping that page hangs the flutter_test isolate, which I verified is PRE-EXISTING by pumping the unmodified HEAD version of the file (both hang identically, ~3.5-10 min, no assertion reached). So the page's inclusion of the widget is verified by reading, not by a test; severing that one line would not fail this test. Shared-file gate: the whole skotiq_core suite ran (5382 passed, 23 failed) and the whole skotiq_app suite ran (2794 passed, 46 failed); every failure is in an untouched area - imaging_service_test (sqlite 'idx_profiles_name already exists' from parallel isolates, the known cold-start flake), nina_sequence_fidelity_test (another agent's in-flight importer validation), and the golden/captures_landscape pixel tests plus a path_provider MissingPluginException.
